answer: Verify each identity against a distinct physical mailing address recorded in an atlas of delivery points: the network mails a one-time quartz-sealed code, and only a reply from that address activates standing. A hollow claim with no real mailbox fails, because mail cannot be delivered to a fake address. An attacker must rent or control one real address per fake, paying postage and facing address-reuse detection, so cost grows with each identity. Limit: shared housing and mail-forwarding services blur one-address-one-person, and privacy suffers.
